items.title: Media Alias Display - Moderately critical - Information disclosure - SA-CONTRIB-2026-292
items.summary:
Project: 
Media Alias Display
Project machine name: 
media_alias_display
Date: 
2026-October-28
Security risk: 
Moderately critical 11 ∕ 25 AC:Complex/A:None/CI:Some/II:None/E:Proof/TD:Uncommon
Vulnerability: 
Information disclosure
Affected versions: 
<2.1.3 || >=3.0.0 <3.0.3
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-118571
Description: 

This module allows for direct viewing of a file with the URL alias.

This is a followup advisory to SA-CONTRIB-2026-245, which did not fully resolve the underlying vulnerability.

In some cases, files may be served with the HTTP header Cache-Control: public when they should be uncacheable. This can lead to some users getting cached versions of files with information they should not be able to access.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the following:

  • Drupal must be configured to handle non-public files using a custom or contributed module providing an additional file scheme.
  • An attacker must know to request a file that has previously been requested by a more-privileged user, and that file must still be cached.
Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • If you use version 3.0.x, upgrade to 3.0.3.
  • If you use version 2.1.x, upgrade to 2.1.3.

The module did not sufficiently encrypt the password of the system user used when synchronizing content. This can potentially allow unprivileged users to view the password.

items.title: OAuth2 Token Manager - Critical - Access bypass - SA-CONTRIB-2026-290
items.summary:
Project: 
OAuth2 Token Manager
Project machine name: 
oauth2_token_manager
Date: 
2026-October-28
Security risk: 
Critical 15 ∕ 25 AC:Complex/A:None/CI:Some/II:Some/E:Theoretical/TD:All
Vulnerability: 
Access bypass
Affected versions: 
<1.2.0
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-118573
Description: 

This module lets you manage system-wide OAuth2 access and refresh tokens for Box, Quip, and Slack integrations through Drush and an OAuth2 validation callback.

The module doesn't restrict access to its OAuth2 routes, allowing an an anonymous visitor to potentially connect the site's integration to an account they control.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that an attacker must obtain the OAuth2 state value from a previous system token initialization (for example, from the server access logs).

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • If you use the OAuth2 Token Manager module, upgrade to OAuth2 Token Manager 8.x-1.2

After updating, run database updates. If you suspect your Box, Quip or Slack integration was connected to an unauthorized account, re-initialize the system token with Drush.

items.title: Field Permissions - Moderately critical - Access bypass - SA-CONTRIB-2026-289
items.summary:
Project: 
Field Permissions
Project machine name: 
field_permissions
Date: 
2026-October-28
Security risk: 
Moderately critical 13 ∕ 25 AC:None/A:None/CI:Some/II:None/E:Theoretical/TD:Uncommon
Vulnerability: 
Access bypass
Affected versions: 
<1.6.0
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-118584
Description: 

The Field Permissions module enables you to set field-level permissions for viewing and editing fields, including a "Private" setting.

The module does not sufficiently restrict access to "Private" fields on entity types that have no field for an author (user account or owner). As a result, a field configured as "Private" on one of these entities can be viewed. Where the entity is editable, the entity can also be edited by anyone who can view it, including anonymous users.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that an administrator must have configured a field as "Private" on an entity type that has no author, and the attacker must already be able to view that entity. Fields set to "Private" on nodes, users, media, comments, and other entity types with an author are not affected. Fields using Custom permissions are not affected.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • If you use the Field Permissions module for Drupal 9.5, 10 or 11, upgrade
    to Field Permissions 8.x-1.6.

items.title: OpenID Connect Client - Moderately critical - Improper authentication - SA-CONTRIB-2026-287
items.summary:
Project: 
OpenID Connect Client
Project machine name: 
oidc
Date: 
2026-October-28
Security risk: 
Moderately critical 14 ∕ 25 AC:Basic/A:None/CI:Some/II:Some/E:Theoretical/TD:Uncommon
Vulnerability: 
Improper authentication
Affected versions: 
<2.3.1
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-118554
Description: 

The module enables authentication via the OpenID Connect (oAuth2) protocol.

When a new user logs in via OpenID Connect, the module tries to link the user to an existing account with the same email address. Doing so it allows to take over any existing Drupal account (except user 1) that has not yet been linked to an OpenID Connect user.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that the site must be configured to use a provider that doesn't verify the email address of the user.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • Upgrade to OpenID Connect Client 2.3.1.

Linking new users to an existing account is now disabled by default and can be re-enabled on the settings page. When using a generic realm it's also highly recommended to configure the email verified claim.

Reported By: 
  • Sanjeev Kumar (ksanjeev284)
Fixed By: 
  • Matthijs Van Assche (matthijs)

The module doesn't sufficiently check file URL for malicious content when attempting to do fallback retrieval leading to a cross-site scripting vulnerability.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact this development module must be enabled on an attacker's target site, and the attacker must be able to upload a malicious file to the "origin" server configured for the module.

items.title: S3 File System - Moderately critical - Access bypass - SA-CONTRIB-2026-279
items.summary:
Project: 
S3 File System
Project machine name: 
s3fs
Date: 
2026-October-28
Security risk: 
Moderately critical 14 ∕ 25 AC:Complex/A:None/CI:Some/II:Some/E:Theoretical/TD:Default
Vulnerability: 
Access bypass
Affected versions: 
<3.12.0
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-118574
Description: 

S3 File System (s3fs) provides an additional file system to your Drupal site that stores files in Amazon's Simple Storage Service (S3) storage.

The module doesn't sufficiently isolate upload context between separate object(file) operations in the same request resulting in the potential for objects to be uploaded with incorrect access control list (ACL) entries or corruption through incorrect operation metadata.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that an attacker must be able to trigger multiple file operations on S3FS.

Some vectors are mitigated by:

  • Not enabling private:// takeover ($settings['s3fs.use_s3_for_private'] = FALSE;) or only enabled with $settings['s3fs.upload_as_private'] = TRUE;
  • The deployment does not utilize hook_s3fs_stream_open_params_alter(), hook_s3fs_upload_params_alter(), hook_s3fs_copy_params_alter(), or hook_s3fs_command_params_alter()

If both points above have always been true, all currently known vectors are mitigated.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • If you use the S3 File System module for Drupal 8.x, upgrade to s3fs 8.x-3.12

If private:// takeover is enabled without $settings['s3fs.upload_as_private'] = TRUE; audit all private object ACL's to ensure no objects include a public read ACL entry. If private objects with public read ACL are discovered, audit S3 Bucket Access logs (if enabled).

If using S3FS hooks, audit all objects to ensure any applied customization is reflected only on the intended objects.

While auditing objects, site owners may disable ACLs and utilize a Bucket Access Policy to block public access to private:// files. See the s3fs 8.x-3.12 README.txt for a sample policy. $settings['s3fs.use_s3_for_private'] = TRUE; must be configured prior to disabling ACLs.

Note: With ACLs disabled, the S3 getObjectAcl call will not report ACL entries. If this feature is enabled, consider utilizing an AWS S3 Inventory report to obtain object metadata.

Security risk: 
Moderately critical 13 ∕ 25 AC:Basic/A:None/CI:None/II:Some/E:Theoretical/TD:All
Vulnerability: 
Cross-Site Request Forgery
Affected versions: 
<4.1.1
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-118570
Description: 

This module enables you to quickly toggle the publication status, promotion and stickiness of nodes, and the publication status of comments, from links on the page.

The module doesn't sufficiently protect against cross-site request forgery (CSRF) on its toggle URL, under the scenario where a user with the "Use Fasttoggle" permission visits a page controlled by an attacker while logged in. This allows the attacker to change the publication status of arbitrary content on behalf of that user.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that an attacker must trick a user with the permission "Use Fasttoggle" into visiting an attacker-controlled page.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • If you use the Fasttoggle module, upgrade to Fasttoggle 4.1.1

items.title: CAPTCHA - Moderately critical - Session Replay (CAPTCHA bypass) - SA-CONTRIB-2026-281
items.summary:
Project: 
CAPTCHA
Project machine name: 
captcha
Date: 
2026-October-28
Security risk: 
Moderately critical 13 ∕ 25 AC:Basic/A:None/CI:None/II:None/E:Exploit/TD:All
Vulnerability: 
Session Replay (CAPTCHA bypass)
Affected versions: 
<1.18.0 || >=2.0.0 <2.0.11
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-118582
Description: 

The CAPTCHA module places a configurable challenge on forms to block automated submissions. To skip the challenge on later steps of the same multi-step form, the module remembers that a CAPTCHA session has been solved.

The module does not fully invalidate a solved CAPTCHA session. As a result, a protected form that was already submitted once can be submitted again without solving a new CAPTCHA. This weakens the protection the module provides against automated submissions such as spam registrations, comment spam, and login brute-forcing.

This is a follow-up to the earlier CAPTCHA replay fix (SA-CONTRIB-2026-015 / CVE-2026-3214), which closed one replay path but left this one open.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

    • If you use the Captcha module 2.0.x, upgrade to Captcha 2.0.11.
    • If you use the Captcha module 8.x-1.x, upgrade to Captcha 8.x-1.18.

items.title: Single Content Sync - Critical - External control of file name or path - SA-CONTRIB-2026-274
items.summary:
Project: 
Single Content Sync
Project machine name: 
single_content_sync
Date: 
2026-October-28
Security risk: 
Critical 17 ∕ 25 AC:Basic/A:Admin/CI:All/II:All/E:Theoretical/TD:All
Vulnerability: 
External control of file name or path
Affected versions: 
<1.4.19
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-118561
Description: 

Single Content Sync enables exporting and importing content, referenced entities, and files between Drupal sites.

The module does not sufficiently validate file sources and destinations during content imports. An attacker can write arbitrary files, disclose sensitive local files accessible to the web server, or cause the server to make requests to internal or external resources. Depending on the server configuration, this may lead to remote code execution.

Exploitation requires the import single content permission. This permission is marked as restricted starting with version 1.4.18. Remote code execution additionally depends on the server permitting execution of attacker-controlled files.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • If you use the Single Content Sync module, upgrade to Single Content Sync 1.4.19.

Run database updates and rebuild caches after upgrading. Review the module permissions and ensure only highly trusted roles have the "import single content" permission.

Remote file downloads during imports are disabled by default. Sites that require this functionality must configure trusted file hosts in the module settings. Alternatively, import ZIP files containing the required assets.

Security risk: 
Less critical 8 ∕ 25 AC:Complex/A:User/CI:Some/II:None/E:Theoretical/TD:Uncommon
Vulnerability: 
Information Disclosure
Affected versions: 
<1.4.11 || >=1.5.0 <1.5.2
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-118551
Description: 

This module provides a framework for integrating AI providers and features into Drupal.

Audio for every speech-to-text request is written to the same file in the temporary directory and does not delete it afterwards. As a result, an attacker who can read the site's temporary directory could get the audio that another user sent for transcription.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that the attacker needs read access to the temporary directory, either through the server (for example a shared hosting account) or through a module or custom code that exposes temporary files to other users. Drupal core's system.temporary route only serves temporary files to the user who owns them.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • If you use version 1.5.x, upgrade to AI 1.5.2.
  • If you use version 1.4.x, upgrade to AI 1.4.11.
  • If you use version 1.3.x, upgrade to AI 1.5.2 or AI 1.4.11 as the 1.3.x branch is now unsupported.

The fix keeps the audio in memory and no longer writes it to the temporary directory. Site owners may also want to delete any leftover speech_to_text.mp3 file in the temporary directory.

items.title: AI (Artificial Intelligence) - Moderately critical - Access bypass - SA-CONTRIB-2026-270
items.summary:
Project: 
AI (Artificial Intelligence)
Project machine name:

Date: 
2026-October-28
Security risk: 
Moderately critical 10 ∕ 25 AC:Complex/A:None/CI:Some/II:None/E:Theoretical/TD:Uncommon
Vulnerability: 
Access bypass
Affected versions: 
<1.4.11 || >=1.5.0 <1.5.2
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-118550
Description: 

This module provides a framework for integrating Drupal with AI providers. Its AI Search submodule provides a Search API backend that stores content in a vector database for semantic search.

The AI Search submodule has always been marked as 'experimental' but more importantly is deprecated. You may wish to use this as an opportunity to move to the standalone AI Search which is a drop-in replacement and target of all new development. It also had the same vulnerability.

The AI Search backend checks access to each search result for the current user, but this is not taken into account when Search API caches the results of a view. As a result, cached search results, including titles and other displayed fields of unpublished or access-restricted content, can be shown to users who do not have access to that content in some configurations.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that:

  • The AI Search submodule must be enabled and used with a Search API view.
  • The view must use Search API result caching ("Search API (time-based)", "Search API (tag-based)" or "Search API (time and tag-based)"). The default, "Search API (none)", is not affected.
  • A user with access to the restricted content must have run the same search within the cache lifetime.

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) tools, AI Assistant RAG actions and custom code running Search API queries are not affected.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • If you use the AI module 1.5.x with the AI Search submodule, upgrade to AI 1.5.2
  • If you use the AI module 1.4.x with the AI Search submodule, upgrade to AI 1.4.11
  • If you use the AI module 1.3.x with the AI Search submodule, upgrade to AI 1.5.2 or AI 1.4.11 as the 1.3.x branch is now unsupported.
  • If you use the AI Search 1.3.x standalone module, upgrade to AI 1.3.0-alpha6
  • If you use the AI Search 2.0.x standalone module, upgrade to AI 2.0.0-alpha3
